specPoints.text: know what is meant by the terms: solvent, solute, solution, saturated solution

primer.text: Everyday life already teaches this note: stirring sugar into tea or salt into soup shows something vanishing into a liquid. That liquid, that vanished substance and the resulting mixture each carry a precise name, and this note fixes the vocabulary — solvent, solute, solution, saturated solution, soluble, insoluble — using sea water, where all of them appear at once.

lessons.title: Solutions Terminology
lessons.opening: Dissolving has a vocabulary of its own, and every term in it names a role. Sea water carries the whole set in one example: the water is the solvent, the salt is the solute, and the mixture itself is the solution. Add enough salt and the water refuses to take more — the saturated state — which the Dead Sea shows on a grand scale.
keyPoints: The solvent is the liquid doing the dissolving; in sea water it is the water.
The solute is the substance that dissolves; in sea water it is the salt.
A solution is the mixture formed once a solute has dissolved in a solvent.
A saturated solution holds the maximum amount of dissolved solute the solvent can take, as with sea water in the Dead Sea.
Soluble describes a substance that will dissolve, and insoluble describes one that will not, like sand in water.

low.restatement: Six terms describe dissolving. The solvent is the liquid, the solute is what dissolves in it, and the solution is the mixture you get; saturated means no more solute can dissolve, while soluble and insoluble record whether something dissolves at all.
low.analogy: Making a cup of tea: the hot water is the solvent, the sugar is the solute, the sweet drink is the solution — and once sugar piles up undissolved at the bottom, the cup is saturated.
low.examPointer: Definition questions are free marks when the terms are precise: learn each one with its single-line meaning and a sea-water example.

medium.restatement: In a solution the solvent is the liquid doing the dissolving and the solute is the substance dissolved in it; the solution is the mixture that results. A saturated solution carries the greatest amount of dissolved solute possible, and soluble or insoluble records whether a substance will dissolve.
medium.analogy: A rush-hour bus: the bus is the solvent, the passengers are the solute, the loaded bus is the solution, and when nobody else can board, it is saturated.
medium.examPointer: Expect a match-the-term item or a definition with a missing word; quote the term exactly (saturated solution, not saturated liquid) and attach the sea-water or Dead Sea example where it fits.

check.stem: In sea water, which term names the salt?

options.explanation: The salt is the substance that dissolves, which is exactly the solute's role.
The solvent is the liquid doing the dissolving; in sea water that is the water, not the salt.
options.misconception: swaps the roles of solute and solvent

options.explanation: The solution is the whole mixture of salt and water together, not the salt on its own.
options.misconception: names the mixture rather than the dissolved substance

options.explanation: Saturation describes a solution holding the maximum dissolved solute; it is not a name for the salt itself.
options.misconception: attaches saturation to any dissolved substance

check.stem: A solution holding the greatest amount of dissolved solute it can is called...

options.explanation: Saturation means no more solute can dissolve; the solution is full to its limit.
Insoluble means a substance will not dissolve at all; saturation is about having dissolved the maximum already.
The solvent is only the liquid; saturation describes the state of the whole solution.
options.misconception: applies a component term to the whole mixture

options.explanation: Dilute describes a solution with little solute, the opposite of saturated.

check.stem: Sand sits in a beaker of water without dissolving. Which term describes the sand?

options.explanation: A substance that will not dissolve is insoluble, exactly as the note's example records for sand.
Soluble means able to dissolve; the sand demonstrably has not.
options.misconception: reverses the term for a non-dissolving substance

options.explanation: The solvent is the liquid; the sand is the solid sitting in it.
options.misconception: uses the liquid's term for the solid

options.explanation: Saturation describes how much has dissolved in the solution, not a substance that refuses to dissolve.
options.misconception: applies a mixture-level term to a single substance

check.stem: Which pairing of term and sea-water example is correct?

options.text: Solvent — the water in sea water
options.explanation: The water is the liquid doing the dissolving, which is the solvent's definition.

options.text: Solute — the water in sea water
options.explanation: The water does the dissolving; the salt, not the water, is the solute.
options.misconception: assigns the solvent's example to the solute

options.text: Solution — the salt on its own
options.explanation: The solution is the whole mixture, salt and water together.
options.misconception: names only part of the mixture as the solution

options.explanation: The note's saturation example is sea water in the Dead Sea, water already holding its maximum salt.
options.misconception: treats any natural water as saturated

check.stem: Which statement about the four terms is true?
check.misconceptionClass: relational understanding of the term set

options.text: The solute dissolves in the solvent to form the solution
options.explanation: This is the relationship the definitions build: solute plus solvent gives the solution.

options.text: The solvent dissolves in the solute to form the solution
options.explanation: The roles are reversed: the liquid is never the substance that disappears.
options.misconception: reverses solute and solvent in the relationship

options.text: A saturated solution can still dissolve more solute at the same temperature
options.explanation: Saturated means the maximum is already dissolved; nothing more fits at that temperature.
options.misconception: misses the maximum limit in the saturation definition

options.text: Soluble substances never take part in solutions
options.explanation: Soluble substances are precisely the ones that dissolve to form solutions.

glossary.definition: The liquid that does the dissolving; in sea water the solvent is the water.
The substance that dissolves in the liquid; in sea water the solute is the salt.
The mixture formed once a solute has dissolved in a solvent; sea water is the example.
A solution holding the greatest amount of dissolved solute the solvent can take, such as sea water in the Dead Sea.
Describing a substance that is able to dissolve, like salt in water.
Describing a substance that is unable to dissolve, like sand in water.

workedExample.prompt: A learner stirs salt and sand into a beaker of water. The salt disappears into the water but the sand settles on the bottom. Name: a) the role of the water, b) the role of the salt, c) the mixture formed once the salt has dissolved, d) the term describing the sand.
steps: a) The water is the solvent: the liquid doing the dissolving.
b) The salt is the solute: the substance that dissolves in the liquid to form the mixture.
c) Once the solute has dissolved in the solvent, the mixture is called the solution.
d) The sand does not dissolve, so it is insoluble.
workedExample.finalAnswer: a) Solvent. b) Solute. c) Solution. d) Sand is insoluble.
